crossing supervisor Listen Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Print Content components School crossing supervisors have a much-valued role in Boroondara. On an average school day in Boroondara, they help 9,266 pedestrians to cross the street while 74,426 motor vehicles use our roads during school crossing times. We are always looking for school crossing supervisors. If you are friendly, reliable and flexible, this role is for you. What does a school crossing supervisor do? This paid position gives you the opportunity to get involved in your community and improve road safety for children, people with a disability and the general public who use our 114 school crossings. School crossing supervisors: • work part-time Monday to Friday, from 8 am to 9 am and from 3 pm to 4 pm, during the school term • play an important role in educating children with ‘Stop, Look and Listen’ instructions • are responsible for reporting any road hazards or potential risks • help to encourage active and independent travel. About you We are looking for people aged 18 and older who: • can attend shifts at short notice • have their own reliable transport • are able to work across several locations • can complete the pre-employment medical and police checks. You will have access to a full training program before starting your role. Submit an online application through our Careers website . Attend an interview – meet with one of our Council Officers at Council, located at 8 Inglesby Road in Camberwell. Provide us with relevant employment documents – including your Working With Children Check, Police Check and evidence of your COVID-19 vaccination status. Complete a medical assessment. Apply to become a School Crossings Supervisor We are always recruiting new school crossing supervisors to help people to cross our roads safely at peak school times. Skip to Main Content Career Opportunities: Park Asset Specialist (15178) Requisition ID 15178 - Posted - Job Function (2) - Tenure Status (1) - Employment Status (1)  Job Description Print Preview Apply Save Job Email Job to Friend Return to List $73,273 to $78,901 (ongoing, full time, plus superannuation, 9 day fortnight) Build and maintain the parks and playgrounds that our community enjoys every day Work outdoors across some of Melbourne's most valued parks and reserves The Role Reporting to the Parks Team Leader, the Park Asset Specialist plays an important role in maintaining the safety, functionality and presentation of Council's playgrounds, park furniture and associated infrastructure. Based at Kew Depot and working across the municipality, this hands-on role is responsible for delivering maintenance and repair services that ensure our parks and open spaces remain safe, attractive and welcoming for the community. You will undertake a variety of maintenance activities, inspections and repair works while working collaboratively with colleagues, contractors and members of the public. Key Responsibilities Carry out maintenance, repairs and minor construction works across playgrounds, park furniture and fence assets within Council's open spaces. Undertake routine playground inspections and audits to ensure compliance with relevant Australian Standards and identify any safety concerns. Arrange for hazards and defects to be repaired, replaced or made safe in a timely manner, ensuring community safety remains a priority. Plan and complete maintenance works while considering the horticultural amenity and presentation of park sites, leaving work areas clean and safe upon completion . About You You will bring practical experience in outdoor maintenance, construction, landscaping, carpentry or a related field, together with a strong commitment to safety and high-quality workmanship. You have experience installing, repairing and maintaining outdoor furniture, structures or timber assets and enjoy working in a physically active outdoor environment. You are self-motivated, organised and capable of managing your workload while responding to changing priorities. Your ability to work both independently and as part of a team, combined with strong communication skills, will enable you to build positive relationships with colleagues and the community. Qualifications or experience in carpentry, landscaping, welding, forklift operation or medium rigid vehicle operation will be highly regarded. For more information regarding the role, please refer to the attached position description. About Boroondara The City of Boroondara is home to some of Melbourne's most beautiful parks, playgrounds, gardens and open spaces. We are committed to creating a healthy, connected and sustainable community and delivering services that place our customers at the centre of everything we do. As one of Melbourne's most desirable municipalities, we take pride in maintaining high quality public spaces that support recreation, wellbeing and community connection. Working with us means contributing to assets and environments that are enjoyed by thousands of residents and visitors each year. Employment Requirements Applicants must hold unrestricted working rights in Australia, and those progressing through the selection process will need to complete a National Police Record Check, a Working with Children Check and relevant pre-employment medical assessments. How to Apply Please submit your application online via the 'Apply' button by 11.59pm, Sunday 23 August 2026. All applications must be made via the online portal; no applications direct to the hiring manager or from recruitment agencies will be considered. Skip to Main Content Career Opportunities: Digital Marketing Officer (15171) Requisition ID 15171 - Posted - Job Function (1) - Tenure Status (1) - Employment Status (1)  Job Description Print Preview Apply Save Job Email Job to Friend Return to List Help strengthen our social media and email newsletters to drive positive outcomes for the community Flexible, supportive hybrid work environment Salary $104,790 - $114,015 per annum plus super and RDO We’re looking for a Digital Marketing Officer to bring the City of Boroondara's programs, services and stories to life through engaging social media and e-newsletter content. You’ll use your creativity, multimedia capabilities and communications skills to help us inform, engage and support our community. A little bit about the role The Digital Marketing Officer supports the Strategic Communications department to ensure Council’s digital marketing activities are effective, and Council’s social media and email newsletters are driving positive community outcomes. This role reports to the Digital Marketing Lead and works with internal stakeholders across Council to deliver campaigns, produce platform appropriate multimedia content and use performance insights to continually improve Council’s digital communications. The Digital Marketing Officer plays an integral role in helping Council connect with the community through timely, accessible and engaging content. Key responsibilities include: Plan and produce platform appropriate content, including video, photography and written content for social media and email newsletters. Work with internal partners to deliver digital marketing campaigns that are informed by customer insights, data, market trends and best-practice approaches. Write, edit and publish accessible digital content that provides a positive customer experience. Maintain publishing schedules and ensure Council’s digital channels remain active, timely and aligned with community interests. Monitor and moderate community interactions across digital channels in line with Council policies and agreed processes. Use analytics and reporting to measure performance, identify trends and recommend improvements. Manage digital marketing activity (paid and organic), including campaign setup, audience targeting, budget monitoring and performance optimisation. Provide digital communications advice, training and input to support continuous improvement across Council A little bit about you You will have proven ability to engage and grow audiences on social media, underpinned by a deep knowledge of social media platforms, contemporary content approaches, creative trends and audience behaviour. You have demonstrated experience producing multimedia content for social media and email newsletter audiences reflecting platform specific aesthetics and viewer preferences. You will have demonstrated experience working in a multi-stakeholder environment developing marketing strategies and delivering digital marketing campaigns. You will be a confident communicator with strong writing skills and the ability to build effective relationships throughout the organisation. You will have the ability to use digital analytics to gather information and identify insights and moderate digital channels and manage online community interactions to deliver the best possible customer outcomes. You will also bring tertiary qualifications in marketing, media, communications or a related discipline, or relevant professional experience in a similar role. Want to know more You can connect further and gain a better insight into this opportunity by reviewing the Position Description Employment requirements Applicants must have the right to work in Australia Preferred applicants will be required to undergo a National Police Record Check How to apply If you are a creative digital communicator who knows how to turn ideas into engaging online content, we’d love to hear from you. Please submit your application online via the ‘Apply’ button. All applications must be made via our online portal by Sunday 9 August 2026. No applications direct to the hiring manager or from recruitment agencies will be considered. To support your application, please share samples of your work as part of your cover letter which demonstrates your ability to produce social media appropriate content that engages audiences. Child Safety Commitment at Alpine Shire Council Alpine Shire Council is committed to being a child safe organisation. Every child and young person has the right to feel safe. All our employees have a shared responsibility to protect children and young people from harm and abuse. Alpine Shire Council have established policies, procedures and training to achieve these commitments. Diversity & Inclusivity at Alpine Shire Council Alpine Shire Council is an Equal Opportunity employer. We value people of all abilities, people from culturally and/or linguistically diverse backgrounds and First Nations peoples. We are committed to upholding a safe, inclusive and respectful workplace that values the contribution of all. POSITION OVERVIEW The immunisations team work to promote and maintain high standards of public health and wellbeing within our community, with a focus on disease and illness prevention. You will provide an efficient, responsive and responsible service. You will be required to promote the Alpine Shire Council as a customer-focused organisation at all times. You will undertake key responsibilities in a professional, efficient and timely manner, and contribute to Council’s aim of being a high performing organisation. You will need to be passionate and multi-skilled and able to consistently deliver at high standard operational services in a tidy, organised, caring and safe environment. You will contribute towards the public health agenda by improving health outcomes for our children, young people and our community. Reports to: Maternal and Child Health Nurse Coordinator. Immunisations • Administer vaccines at immunisation sessions as required and in accordance with the National Immunisation Program requirements and National Immunisations Framework for Health Professionals. • Assist to ensure accurate recording of all relevant client information. • Ensure the confidentiality of client information is maintained as required. • Ensure the safe keeping of materials and equipment. • Equipment and resources are managed effectively to reduce waste and promote cost efficiency. • Provide assistance with determining an efficient annual schedule of immunisations for Alpine Shire, including: immunisations for 0-5 year old children, the secondary school program, Council staff and older eligible adult influenza vaccine sessions. • Maintain a constant drive towards service improvement. Other duties • Ensure all processing and tasks undertaken are efficient. • Display a punctual, reliable and positive approach to work. • Continually review and improve work methods associated with this role. • Undertake other duties as directed by the manager or supervisor. • In addition to the responsibilities described in this document, all employees must comply with the Alpine Shire Council’s Code of Conduct and Corporate Policies. Judgement and decision making • Guidance is always available from immediate supervisor or manager • The particular tasks to be performed may involve selection from a • limited range of existing techniques, systems, equipment, methods or processes in a defined range of recurring work situations. Management skills • Ability to manage your time and plan your day to achieve specific and set objectives. Interpersonal skills • Good oral and written communication skills with customers, other employees and members of the public and in the resolution of minor problems. • Display a punctual, reliable and positive approach to work • Ability to project a positive image in communicating with both internal and external customers at all times EXPERTISE Essential Qualifications • Victorian driver licence. • Current and valid nursing registration with the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation (AHPRA). • Authorised Immunisation provider. • Working with Children Check. Experience • Previous experience in delivering immunisations and good working knowledge about the National Immunisation Program. Specialist Skills and Knowledge • Understanding of the role including relevant frameworks and guidelines. • Undertaking any personal development as required of registrations and/or as changes are required of the National Immunisation Program. • Sound written and verbal communication skills. • Keen interest and knowledge of vaccine preventable diseases of public health significance and immunisation. • Capacity to prioritise, organise individual work plan and to work semi- autonomously. • Capacity to communicate confidently and independently with senior health professionals and members of the public. HEALTH, SAFETY AND RISK DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES Nothing is more important than the health and safety of yourself and those around you. Smoking is an issue for both Council and employees as it impacts on both the work and personal life of the smoker and other employees and in some cases the reputation of the Council.
